about: J and the separator it inserts. Measured 2026-11-13: a space is added ONLY when the line joined into has no trailing blank of its own - an existing space or tab already separates, and vim does not add a second one. vim and nvi agree on every case here; busybox always inserts a space (it replaces the newline with ' ' and then eats the next line's leading blanks), so these run vim+nvi and busybox stays the scope oracle. The '. ' case carries options.joinspaces=false because vim's own default in this harness inserts TWO spaces after a sentence-ending punctuation; nvi never does, and this engine implements the nojoinspaces rule (the option is not in DECISIONS' :set surface). The visual-mode cases (vjJ, VjjJ, VGJ) run vim-only: neither nvi nor busybox joins a visual selection.

cases.name: a plain join adds one space
a trailing space is the separator: no second one
two trailing spaces are kept, and none is added
a trailing tab is the separator
an existing space plus the next line's indent still gives one
no trailing blank: the next line's indent is dropped and one space added
after a full stop only one space, because joinspaces is off
joining into a blank line adds no space at all
joining a blank line away keeps the first line's trailing space
visual J over two lines, line already ends in a space
...with two trailing spaces they are kept
visual J over a linewise range joins them all
